lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The key sticks, then gives. Grandma's Corner Shop smells of dust, old flour and, somehow, still a little of cinnamon.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the counter, under a jar of wooden spoons, sits an envelope with your name on it in her loopy handwriting.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: My dear, if you're reading this, the shop is yours. Don't let the cobwebs frighten you. They're mostly decorative.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: My recipes are scattered about. I never did like keeping things in one place. Bake, and you'll find them.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Start small. Wheat from the mill, milk from the fridge. Put two good things together and they become something better.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Taped to the window is a glossy flyer: "MegaBun Corp is EXCITED to explore SYNERGIES with this Premium Location!"

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: P.S. If a man in a suit offers to buy the place, offer him a scone instead. It confuses them.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You roll up your sleeves. First things first: those cobwebs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A man in a salt-stiff coat stops at the freshly washed window and peers in, like he's checking the weather.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Lights on, window clean. Thought I was seeing things. Nobody's baked in here since your gran.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: I'm Gus. Boat's the green one by the harbor wall. Out at four, back by ten, hungry as a gull.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Your gran kept a loaf by for me every morning. Never asked. Just knew.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: If there's bread again, I'll be back. Every day. You can set your clock by me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gus is now a regular. He'll place orders at the counter.

lines.speaker: edith
lines.text: Is that stool fixed? Good. It wobbled for eleven years. I counted. Old habit, from teaching.

lines.speaker: edith
lines.text: Forty years of eighth graders, and I survived every one of them on your grandmother's croissants.

lines.speaker: edith
lines.text: She said the trick was cold butter and patience. She had plenty of one and pretended to have the other.

lines.speaker: edith
lines.text: I'm Edith. Miss Edith, to anyone who ever handed in homework late.

lines.speaker: edith
lines.text: I'll expect a croissant on Thursdays. A dough ball, a butter block, a warm oven. You'll get there.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Miss Edith is now a regular.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The bell jingles. A young man in a MegaBun polo shirt freezes in the doorway, then quickly zips up his jacket.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: Hi! Just browsing. Totally normal person. Not affiliated with any large bread-adjacent corporation.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He breathes in. His eyes close. For a moment he looks like someone remembering a better childhood.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: Is that real butter? We have a flavor packet that's supposed to taste like that. It does not.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: I'm Dex. I should go. My manager thinks I'm at a "competitive landscape offsite."

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: But I'll be back. For research. Strictly research. Maybe save me a croissant?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Dex is now a regular. He seems very bad at being a spy.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: The awning! You fixed the awning! I've looked at that sad, flappy thing from my window for three years.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: I'm Mina, from the flower shop next door. Well. Flower stand. It's a very ambitious bucket.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: A MegaBun rep came by my stand too. Asked if I'd "consider a lifestyle partnership." I gave him a daisy.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: This street needs you open. When people buy bread, they buy flowers. It's science. Probably.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: Put me down for a flour sack a week. I'm learning to bake. Badly, but with feeling.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mina is now a regular.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Behind the frame's backing, something crinkles: a folded page, smudged with butter, in Grandma's hand.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Found it! I hid the first one well, didn't I? Your mother never found a single one. You were always the curious one.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Croissants aren't difficult. They're patient. Fold the butter in, rest, fold again. Never rush the dough.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: The rest of my recipes are out there. Follow your customers. They'll lead you to them. They always led me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The page goes into the Recipe Book, right at the front.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sign swings in the morning breeze: RISE & SHINE BAKERY. Open.

lines.speaker: gus
lines.text: Ten o'clock sharp. Told you I'd be here. Is that a sourdough? Don't answer. I'm buying it.

lines.speaker: edith
lines.text: It smells exactly the way it used to. I may cry. I'll deny it if anyone asks.

lines.speaker: mina
lines.text: I brought flowers for the counter! And a friend. And her aunt. Word travels on this street.

lines.speaker: dex
lines.text: I brought nothing, because officially I was never here. One croissant, please.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A courier arrives with an enormous gift basket. The card is printed on very expensive paper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: "MegaBun Corp congratulates this Legacy Micro-Bakery on its Relaunch Journey. We look forward to acquiring—" The rest is smudged.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Inside the basket: six loaves of Artisanal Bread Product™. Contains up to 40% bread.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Tucked under the basket is one more envelope in loopy handwriting.

lines.speaker: grandma
lines.text: Well done, dear. The corner shop is only the beginning. There's a café terrace down the lane that misses me terribly.
